appendices.title: The Two Feeds, Resolution, and Detection Lag
Sample Past Invoices (Sister Program, Other Reserve Sizes)

balance.argument_a: Commercial Weekly's 3 m resolution resolves both size classes of clearing -- it catches all 6.0 ha of confirmed illegal clearing per year, versus Sentinel Free's estimated 3.0 ha (MA6: half of all clearing activity falls below Sentinel Free's 0.09 ha minimum detectable patch size, versus Commercial Weekly's much finer 0.0081 ha floor). Its detection lag is also tighter and faster (median 4 days, range 2-7) than Sentinel Free's (median 8 days, range 3-20), which matters for a field-patrol team trying to respond before a clearing grows.
balance.argument_b: Even after paying for weekly tasking ($15,600/yr) and analyst labor ($2,730/yr, total $18,330), Commercial Weekly's ratio is 0.000327 ha detected per dollar. Sentinel Free costs nothing to download and, once its own analyst labor is counted ($7,665/yr for the extra manual interpretation coarser imagery requires), still detects half the reserve's clearing (3.0 ha) for well under half the price -- a ratio of 0.000391 ha per dollar, 16.4% higher than Commercial Weekly's.
balance.margin_basis: RESOLVED at case-research. total_cost_A = (25 km2 x $12/km2 x 52 weeks) + (52 scenes x 1.5 hr x $35/hr) = $15,600 + $2,730 = $18,330/yr. total_cost_B = 73 scenes x 3.0 hr x $35/hr = $7,665/yr (no subscription fee). det_A = 6.0 ha (all confirmed clearing, both size classes). det_B = 6.0 ha x (1 - 0.50) = 3.0 ha (MA6: half of clearing activity is below Sentinel Free's detection floor). ratio_A = 6.0/18330 = 0.0003273 ha/$. ratio_B = 3.0/7665 = 0.0003914 ha/$. margin = |0.0003914 - 0.0003273| / 0.0003914 = 16.4%. Sentinel Free (Option B) wins, but by 16.4% -- comfortably inside the ~20% cap. The case's real teaching tension is that Commercial Weekly's real detection advantage (it catches strictly more hectares) does not survive being expressed as a cost-adjusted rate once its subscription price is counted in the same units as its benefit -- a student who compares raw hectares detected alone will favor Option A; the ratio favors B.

modeling_assumptions.value_used: 10 values per feed, as tabled in case.md
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public program discloses a real, matched detection-lag data set for two specific commercial-vs-free feeds over the same events. Constructed consistent with each feed's real revisit cadence (weekly tasking vs. ~5-day Sentinel-2 revisit) plus realistic cloud/tasking-gap spread.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Affects D1's spread/median comparison narratively; not an input to D5's ratio or margin_pct.

modeling_assumptions.basis: A representative conservation-sector analyst wage; no single public wage figure was found for this exact role.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Scales both options' labor cost proportionally; does not by itself flip the dilemma.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Commercial Weekly analyst review time per scene
modeling_assumptions.basis: Finer, pre-tasked commercial imagery typically needs less manual interpretation per scene than coarser free imagery.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Sentinel Free analyst review time per scene
modeling_assumptions.basis: Coarser 10 m imagery requires more manual interpretation and cloud-masking work per scene.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: MEDIUM -- a component of total_cost_B; the only real cost Sentinel Free carries.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Total confirmed illegal clearing across the reserve, per year
modeling_assumptions.basis: A representative annual loss figure for a small, actively monitored protected reserve; no public per-reserve figure was found for this specific site.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Scales both options' detected hectares proportionally; does not by itself flip the dilemma.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Share of annual clearing that is 'small' (sub-Sentinel-detectable, super-commercial-detectable)
modeling_assumptions.basis: Informed by published remote-sensing findings that a large share of tropical deforestation now occurs in clearings smaller than moderate-resolution sensors reliably detect.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: HIGH -- this is the case-defining assumption; see the Sensitivity note in case.md Appendix E and sensitivity_model.py's probe-5 sweep.

sensitivity_note: margin_pct (16.4%) is directly and materially sensitive to MA6 (the share of clearing that is sub-Sentinel-detectable). It is comparatively insensitive to MA1, MA2, MA3, MA4, and MA5, which scale both options proportionally or affect only narrative/D1/D3/D4 content without changing the D5 ratio's fundamental structure.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA6 (the 50% share of annual clearing that is sub-Sentinel-detectable) is a stated scenario assumption -- no public, Reserve-specific figure exists for what fraction of this program's real clearing activity falls below Sentinel-2's detection floor. Tier 2 probe 5's +/-50% sweep tests whether a higher or lower share flips the verdict; see QA_REPORT.md for the exact result.
